tender.title: CBC-2192-T-ZH Fire Systems and Equipment Servicing and Maintenance
tender.description:
Central Bedfordshire Council is seeking a suitably qualified and BAFE-registered contractor to provide planned preventative maintenance, inspection, testing, repair and emergency call-out services for fire safety systems and equipment across its housing portfolio. 
Services include fire alarms, dry risers, fire extinguishers, sprinkler and mist systems, fire blankets, and automatic smoke ventilation systems, together with asset management and statutory compliance reporting.

tender.title: CP-401 - Aster Group External Decorations
tender.description:
Aster Group is a housing association which provides quality, affordable homes to thousands of people across the south of England and London. Its vision is that everyone has a home. See our website for more details www.aster.co.uk/corporate/about-us
The not-for-dividend business was established in 1990 and has £2.5 billion worth of social housing assets. The Group reinvests profits from open market sale and shared ownership to support the development of affordable homes. It owns and maintains over 37,000 homes and employs over 2,000 people.
Central and Cecil Housing Trust (C&C), East Boro Housing Trust (EBHT) and Enham Trust form part of the Aster Group. For further information visit: www.ccht.org.uk, www.ebht.org.uk and www.enhamtrust.org.uk.
Aster Group Limited ("Aster") has a requirement for three contractors to provide External Decoration services, including but not limited to:
•	Redecoration of all previously painted external surfaces and internal common parts.
•	Minor external fabric repairs including:
o	Renewal of fascias and soffits where required (to match existing).
o	Renewal of timber canopies where required.
o	Repointing of brick work.
•	Minor prior to paint repairs.
•	Timber window repairs.
•	Renewal of communal floor finishes where required.
Aster's requirement is across its full geographical coverage and will be split into the following lots with the corresponding approx. number of properties:
•	Lot 1 (East)
o	Berkshire - 205
o	Hampshire - 8416
o	Oxfordshire - 612
o	Wiltshire (incl. Gloucestershire) - 8606
•	Lot 2 (London and Outer Areas)
o	London - 1969
o	Surrey - 441
o	Sussex - 736
•	Lot 3 (West)
o	Dorset - 803
o	Somerset (incl. Bristol) - 5339
o	Devon and Cornwall - 3208
NB: The property numbers are approximate and may make up multi dwelling properties.
Suppliers may submit bids for multiple lots; however, only one supplier will be awarded each lot. Where a supplier achieves the highest ranking in more than one lot, Aster Group reserves the right to determine which lot will be awarded to that supplier. In such circumstances, the lot not awarded to the highest-ranked supplier will instead be awarded to the supplier ranked second for that lot.
Aster's procurement for external decorations is anticipated to be a single stage tender process and will be undertaken via CHIC's All Under One Roof' DPS (Lot 20 - Decoration Services).
The evaluation criteria is anticipated to be 60/40 (price/quality).
Aster has a target start date of May 2027, by which point mobilisation should be completed (TUPE is applicable) and contractors are fully onboarded to Aster's Approved Supplier List and familiar with its Contractor Portal. By the contract start date, the contractor should ensure a fully resourced programme is made available to Aster.
The form of contract Aster anticipated to contract with is the JCT Measured Term Contract (2024 edition) containing Aster amendments.

procedure.features:
This procurement procedure follows a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise, undertaken in accordance with Section 6 of the Procurement Act 2023. A summary of the Preliminary Market Engagement exercise is included in the tender documents.
CGA is using the Competitive Flexible Procedure in accordance with section 20(2)(b) the Procurement Act 2023 (the PA2023). Bidders are deemed to understand the processes that CGA is required to follow under the PA2023.
The procedure will consist of the following stages:
Stage 1 – Procurement Specific Questionnaire
Bidders must complete and submit the Procurement Specific Questionnaire (PSQ) – this document. The PSQ sets out the conditions of participation for this procurement and will consist of:
•Pass/fail questions
•Information only questions
•Scored questions
The PSQ will used to determine each Bidder’s eligibility and suitability to perform the Contract
The top 4 scoring Bidders in Stage 1 will be shortlisted to Stage 2 Invitation to Tender.
Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender Stage
The Invitation to Tender (ITT) Stage will be used to evaluate each Bidders detailed proposal to deliver the Contract and will consist of:
oQuality evaluation
      oWritten submission
      oBidder interview
oPricing evaluation
Only short listed Bidders are required to complete and submit the ITT document. The ITT document is made available at the PSQ stage for information only and to enable Bidders to gain an understanding of the ITT process should they be short listed.
Please do not complete or submit the ITT document at the PSQ stage.

tender.title: Vehicle Repairs Service
tender.description:
Lancashire Constabulary’s Fleet Departmentrequire Accident/Collision and Vehicle MechanicalRepair Service to repair and maintain vehicles. TheAuthority is seeking to procure the services ofbetween 5 and 8 suppliers to provide a broad rangeof repairs to Police Vehicles, to support our VehicleMaintenance Strategies over a 2 year period, withthe option to extend for a further 2 years.
The existing Lancashire Constabulary VehicleRepairs Service Framework Agreement is due toexpire 30th September 2027. The Constabulary will be replacing this with a new framework, estimatedto start on 1st October 2027.
The estimated spend for the replacementframework will be in the region of £4 million.
Suppliers will need to be located within a 60-mileradius (via Google Maps) to our Headquarters site(PR4 5SB). This will enable site visits for vehicleinspections and face to face contract managementto take place at a location based within a distancethat would not add unnecessary costs or delay to the service.
This criterion is also essential to meet carbonreduction and net zero targets, in addition to ourobligation to reduce contract costs.
Suppliers outside of the specified radius arepermitted to set up/utilise appropriatesubcontracting arrangements within the radius. Thiscan include the location and use of suitable sub-contractors who may be able to carry out thisservice on behalf of the supplier.
All vehicle repairs shall be completed strictly inaccordance with the vehicle manufacturer's latestrepair methods, technical bulletins, approved repairprocedures and specifications current at the time ofrepair.
Under no circumstances shall repair methods beused that deviate from manufacturer-approvedprocesses unless written approval is obtained fromthe Lancashire Constabulary.
Qualifications that technicians undertaking repairsmust possess include:
• ATA Accreditation (or equivalent).
• Manufacturer-specific training where available.
• Evidence of ongoing CPD and technical updates.
Lancashire Constabulary will be conducting Pre-Market Engagement. Please keep an eye out forthe UK2 Notice, and information included on ourexternal websites.

milestones.description:
Scope of Engagement
The University is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement to better understand the market's capability and capacity to deliver an agile and responsive Occupational Health Service that supports healthcare students in their academic and placement environments protecting student and patient safety.
The University requires comprehensive Occupational Health service provision to support students across a range of healthcare programmes where placement providers, professional bodies, or regulatory requirements necessitate pre-placement health screening, pre-placement clearance, , immunisation reviews, vaccination programmes, fitness to study assessments, and associated occupational health services.
The purpose of this engagement is to inform the University's future procurement strategy and service specification. The University is particularly interested in understanding how suppliers can provide timely, accessible, locally delivered services to students near to the University City Campus in Sunderland whilst maintaining consistent service quality, regulatory compliance, and positive student experience.
The University welcomes responses from organisations capable of delivering some or all of the following services:
•Pre-placement occupational health screening and health declaration reviews.
•Clearance certification and reporting to support placement requirements.
•Fitness to study s and fitness-for-placement assessments. 
•Immunisation reviews and vaccination programmes.
•Blood testing, serology, and associated laboratory services.
•Timely and evidence-based occupational health assessments following referral from programme leaders, placement teams, student support services, or designated University representatives. Assessments should consider the impact of physical health conditions, mental health conditions, neurodiversity, disability, long-term health conditions, and other health-related factors on a student's ability to safely participate in academic learning and clinical placement activities.
•Secure handling and management of sensitive health information.
•Electronic system, which University of Sunderland staff can access to make management referrals and obtain up-to-date information on fit certificates, immunisation records, student appointment history, and relevant student management reports.
•Face-to-face, remote, and digital service delivery options.
Areas of Interest
The University wishes to understand:
•The supplier's ability to provide local access to Occupational Health services across the Northeast.
•Availability of clinic networks, partner arrangements, mobile services, and remote assessment capabilities.
•Capacity to accommodate varying student volumes throughout the academic year, including peak intake periods.
•Typical turnaround times for assessments, testing, vaccination programmes, and clearance certification.
•Approaches to managing urgent or accelerated placement clearance requirements and management referrals.
•Service management, reporting, and contract monitoring capabilities.
•Business continuity and resilience arrangements.
•Pricing and commercial delivery models.
•Electronic management systems / digital platforms for information sharing
•Opportunities for innovation and service improvement.
•Experience supporting Higher Education Institutions and placement-based academic programmes
Supplier Engagement Process
Interested organisations are invited to submit a written response outlining their capability, experience, and approach to delivering the services described within this notice.
Due to resource and time constraints, the University intends to invite a maximum of five (5) suppliers to participate in further market engagement activities. These activities may include supplier presentations, clarification meetings, demonstrations, or structured market engagement workshops.
Where more than five responses are received, the University may shortlist suppliers based on the relevance of their experience, capability to deliver locally accessible services, capacity, and overall suitability to inform the University's future procurement strategy.
The University reserves the right to invite fewer than five suppliers where, in its opinion, insufficient responses are received that demonstrate the required experience, capability, or capacity.
Participation in this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise will not confer any advantage in any future procurement exercise and will not be a prerequisite for participation in any subsequent tender opportunity.
Information Requested from Suppliers
Suppliers responding to this notice are requested to provide:
1.An overview of their organisation and relevant Occupational Health service provision.
2.Details of experience delivering Occupational Health services to Higher Education institutions, healthcare education providers, or other placement-based programmes.
3.Details of geographic coverage, including clinic locations, partner networks, and remote service capabilities.
4.Typical turnaround times for: 
oHealth questionnaire reviews;
oOccupational Health clearance assessments;
oImmunisation reviews;
oBlood testing and laboratory services; and
oIssue of placement clearance certificates
oManagement referrals
5.Capacity to support large student cohorts' intakes throughout an academic year.
6.Examples of management information and reporting available to clients.
7.Information on the Electronic management system / digital platforms used for information sharing 
8.Information on innovative approaches, digital platforms, or service enhancements that may improve efficiency or student experience.
9.Any market considerations, risks, or opportunities that the University should take into account when developing its future procurement strategy.
Your response should be on no more than 4 sides of A4. Saved to PDF
Responses must be submitted to bids@example.org by 12:00 on the 27th of November. 
The University will inform those that have been selected for the interview stage of the Pre Market Engagement by December 4th. Interview stage will take place Thursday 10th. 
This engagement is intended solely to inform the University's understanding of the market and to assist in the development of a future procurement approach. No commitment is being made at this stage to commence a procurement process or award a contract.

tender.title: Provision of Occupational Health Services for healthcare students
tender.description:
The University is seeking to procure a comprehensive Occupational Health Service to support students enrolled on healthcare programmes that include mandatory clinical, practice-based or work placement activities. The service must support compliance with university, placement provider, professional body and regulatory requirements while promoting student wellbeing, fitness to study, and patient safety.
The provider will be required to deliver an agile, responsive and student-focused service, with accessible provision located within reasonable travelling distance of the University of Sunderland and placement locations across the Northeast. Services should be available through a combination of face-to-face, remote and digital delivery models.
The scope of services includes:
•Pre-placement occupational health screening and health declaration reviews.
•Placement clearance assessment, certification and reporting.
•Fitness to study and fitness for placement assessments.
•Occupational health management referrals to support students experiencing physical health conditions, mental health conditions, disability, neurodiversity, long-term health conditions or other circumstances that may impact their ability to participate safely in academic or placement activities.
•Evidence-based recommendations on reasonable adjustments, support measures, placement restrictions and return-to-study arrangements in accordance with the Equality Act 2010.
•Immunisation reviews, vaccination programmes and immunity status management.
•Blood testing, serology and associated laboratory services.
•Occupational health advice, guidance and referral services.
•Mental health and wellbeing assessments where relevant to study or placement activity.
•Secure management of confidential health records and sensitive personal information.
•An electronic case management system enabling authorised University staff to submit referrals, monitor case progress, access clearance certification and immunisation records, and obtain management information reports.
•Service reporting, governance, quality assurance and regulatory compliance.
The University is particularly interested in suppliers' capability and capacity to provide timely service delivery, local clinical access, scalable support during peak student intake periods, robust digital systems, effective contract management arrangements, and innovative approaches that enhance the student experience while maintaining high standards of occupational health practice and patient safety.
